facts.statement: The species Notocaiman stromeri was once considered a synonym of Eocaiman.
The genus Eocaiman is divided into four species, some of which are considered doubtful.
facts.quote: Este género está dividido por 4 especies, de las cuales son dudosas

facts.statement: The holotype AMNH 3158 was found in Argentina and identified as Eocaiman cavernensis, named by Simpson in 1933.
facts.quote: El holotipo AMNH 3158, fue hallado en Argentina, y fue identificado como: Eocaiman cavernensis, nombrado por Simpson, en 1933

facts.statement: The second species was found in the Salamanca Formation in Argentina and identified as Eocaiman palaeocenicus, named by Bona in 2007.
facts.quote: La segunda especie, fue encontrada en la Formación Salamanca, en Argentina. Esta especie fue identificada como: Eocaiman palaeocenicus (MPEF-PV 1933), nombrado por Bona, en 2007

facts.statement: The third species was found in São José de Itabora, Brazil, and identified as Eocaiman itaboraiensis, named by Pinheiro in 2013.
facts.quote: La tercera especie, fue encontrada en São José de Itabora, Brasil. Esta fue identificada como: Eocaiman itaboraiensis (MCT 1791-R), nombrado por Pinheiro, en 2013

facts.statement: An undescribed species was found at the La Venta site in Colombia.
facts.quote: Una especie sin describir, fue encontrada en el yacimiento La Venta, en Colombia

facts.statement: Eocaiman species lived from the Early Paleocene to the Miocene in what is now Argentina, Brazil, and Colombia.
facts.quote: Eocaiman is an extinct genus of caiman containing species living from the Early Paleocene to Miocene in what is now Argentina (Salamanca and Sarmiento Formations), Itaboraí Formation of Brazil and Colombia (Honda Group)

facts.statement: Eocaiman is an extinct genus of South American alligatorid from the Paleocene and Miocene.
facts.quote: Eocaiman es un género extinto de aligatórido de América del Sur, del Paleoceno y el Mioceno

facts.statement: The fossil of Eocaiman cavernensis dates to the Eocene.
The fossil of Eocaiman palaeocenicus dates to the Paleocene.
The fossil of Eocaiman itaboraiensis dates to the Paleocene and Eocene.
facts.quote: Cuyo fósil data del Paleoceno y el Eoceno

facts.statement: The time range for Eocaiman is from the Danian to the Tortonian, spanning 66 to 11 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Tortonian (66 to 11 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eocaiman belongs to the subfamily Caimaninae.
Eocaiman belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
The genus Eocaiman was named by Simpson in 1933.
Eocaiman belongs to the order Crocodilia.
Eocaiman belongs to the class Sauropsida.
Eocaiman belongs to the phylum Chordata.
Eocaiman belongs to the kingdom Animalia.
The parent group of Eocaiman is Globidonta.
Eocaiman is classified as a reptile.
There are 7 recorded fossil occurrences of Eocaiman.
